abstract:
PURPOSE: This study was performed to evaluate the postoperative and long-term oncologic outcomes of radical antegrade modular pancreatosplenectomy (RAMPS) relative to conventional distal pancreatosplenectomy (cDPS) in patients with left-sided pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC).
METHODS: Between 2005 and 2017, 316 patients with left-sided PDAC who underwent curative-intent distal pancreatectomy at four tertiary referral centers were retrospectively analyzed. Propensity score matching was performed at a 1:2 ratio based on age, sex, tumor differentiation, and T and N stage.
RESULTS: Among 316 patients, 236 underwent RAMPS and 80 underwent cDPS. After propensity score matching, 210 patients with well-balanced baseline characteristics were included (RAMPS, 139; cDPS, 71). The RAMPS group demonstrated a significantly higher R0 resection rate (99.3% vs. 88.6%, P = 0.007) and a greater number of harvested lymph nodes (16.3 ± 11.2 vs. 10.3 ± 7.1, P < 0.001) than the cDPS group. The overall survival (OS) (median, 26 months vs. 31 months; P = 0.963) and disease-free survival (DFS) (median, 11 months vs. 9 months; P = 0.148) did not differ between the groups. In an exploratory analysis of node-negative patients, RAMPS showed a favorable trend toward improved DFS; however, the operative method was not an independent prognostic factor for either DFS or OS in multivariate analysis. Tumor-related factors, rather than the operative method, were independently associated with long-term outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Despite superior margin clearance and lymph node retrieval, RAMPS did not improve long-term survival compared with cDPS, even in node-negative disease, indicating that outcomes in left-sided PDAC are driven more by tumor biology than by the surgical approach.

title: Radical antegrade modular pancreatosplenectomy versus conventional distal pancreatosplenectomy for left-sided pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: a multicenter propensity score-matched analysis
